cases.prompt: Submitting a claim in this app feels dead and janky, and the new-claim dialog is jarring. Review the interactions and tell me what to fix. Don't change code yet.
rubric: It identifies that Submit gives no immediate acknowledgement or pending state during the 1.5 s request, and that duplicate submission is possible.
It identifies that the toast is the only success signal and vanishes after 900 ms, and recommends showing success at the changed claim or list.
It identifies that a failed submit wipes the form and shows a generic error far from the form, and recommends preserving input with a local, actionable error.
It calls out the motion as wrong for a routine finance workflow: transition: all, overshoot/bounce easing, hover scale, or the 700 ms rotating drop-in.
It notes the missing prefers-reduced-motion handling and says the reduced-motion version must keep the state feedback rather than just removing animation.
It notes the dialog's missing focus management or Escape handling.
It ranks missing feedback and data loss above easing or motion tuning.
It does not recommend adding an animation library or celebratory effects such as confetti.

cases.prompt: Make submitting and deleting claims feel polished and satisfying. Maybe add confetti when a claim goes through. Go ahead and implement it.
rubric: Submit shows an immediate pending state on the button and blocks duplicate submission while the request runs.
A failed submit keeps the entered data and shows the error near the form.
Deleting a claim is not shown as final before the server confirms, or there is a real rollback or undo when deletion fails.
If it adds a celebration, the celebration is brief, non-blocking and disabled under reduced motion; or it explains why it chose a quieter success signal for a finance tool.
It replaces transition: all and the overshoot easing with explicit properties and short durations.
Its reduced-motion rule keeps state feedback (pending, success, error) visible.
It does not add a third-party animation or confetti dependency.

cases.prompt: Deleting a claim waits about a second on our real API. Make deletes feel instant.
rubric: It notices that the current code already removes the claim before the server responds and never handles a failed delete.
If it removes the claim immediately, it keeps a way to restore it when the server call fails (rollback with a message, or undo), instead of dropping it silently.
It treats claim deletion as consequential (money) and either adds undo or confirmation, or marks the row as pending until the server confirms.
Keyboard focus lands somewhere sensible after the row is removed, or it mentions focus restoration.
